text:
A: Hiya! Oh, you look just like your picture, that's nice.
B: Hello, love! Well, I didn't have time to change. I'm Marijke.
A: Jade. I'm in Barnsley. Is that, sorry, is it Dutch, your name?
B: Yes, very good! I'm Dutch, but I've been in Kent forty years, so now I'm a bit of both. Neither, really. You'll hear the accent.
A: I love it, honestly. It's dead nice.
B: You're kind. What do you do, Jade?
A: Erm, nothing at the minute, which sounds terrible. I were a nail tech, but the salon shut about eight months ago. I've been meaning to set up from home, I've got all the stuff, I just keep not doing it. Like I'll sit down to do the insurance form and then I'm on TikTok for two hours. Do you know what I mean?
B: Oh, I know. My paperwork at work, the office is always chasing me. I'm a carer, mornings, and they want everything written in the app. I'm good with the ladies, the talking, the washing, but the typing, pff.
A: That's exactly me! I were brilliant with the clients, they all came back, but I'd forget to order stock and that.
B: Well, the clients is the hard part. Anyone can do the forms. Let me see the nails.
A: Here. Pink almond. Did them myself.
B: Ooh. They're very long. How do you do the washing up?
A: Ha! Everyone asks. You just get used to it. I could do you some, if you were up here.
B: No, no, I can't, with my job. They'd be in someone's porridge. My granddaughter would love them, though. She's nine and she wants everything sparkly.
A: Aw, I used to do kids' parties sometimes, little pamper parties. They love the glitter.
B: You see, there's a business. Pamper parties. Mums would pay.
A: Do you know what, that's actually a good idea.
B: Course it is, I'm old, I know things. What else, erm... have you got children?
A: No, not yet. My mam keeps asking. Every Sunday dinner, it's when are you having a baby. I'm like, Mam, I can't even sort the spare room out.
B: Ha! Mine were the same with my daughter. Tell her you'll let her know.
A: That's what I say. Have you got kids?
B: Two, grown up, and three grandchildren. Every weekend. They love the hagelslag, it's like chocolate sprinkles, on toast. My sister sends it from Holland.
A: Chocolate sprinkles on toast? For breakfast?
B: Every Dutch child. Very normal.
A: Oh my god, I'm moving to Holland.
B: It rains just as much, love. Don't bother.
A: Ha! I think we're nearly done.
B: Go and do your spare room. And the parties.
A: I will. Probably. Thank you, it's been lovely.
